passage: The exchange students' bus was forty minutes late, so the teachers squeezed the welcome into ten rushed minutes: everyone would stand up and introduce themselves, one by one, in English. Anirban had gone grey. Sumit leaned over. "Want me to say your name for you, or will you?" Anirban whispered, "You. Just the name." When his turn came, Sumit said, "This is Anirban. He builds robots," and Anirban managed a nod and a small wave. Afterwards Sumit bumped his fist. "The wave counted." On the walk home Sumit said carefully, "You missed the last three trips because of this stuff. Would you talk to the counsellor with me? I'll wait outside." Anirban was quiet for a long time. Then: "Okay. Tuesday."

qa.q: How late was the exchange students' bus?
What does Anirban going grey suggest before the introductions?
qa.a: He was frightened of standing up and speaking to the whole group.

qa.q: What choices did Sumit make during and after the welcome?
qa.a: Sumit asked whether to speak for Anirban, said only his name and one detail, praised the wave, and later offered to go with him to the counsellor.

qa.q: What might have happened if Sumit had pushed Anirban to introduce himself?
qa.a: Anirban might have frozen in front of everyone and felt worse, making the next trip even harder.

grounding: In a rushed welcome, a friend speaks for a frightened friend when asked, celebrates a small step and gently suggests the counsellor.

passage: In the Chennai apartment complex, the Independence Day programme was all anyone talked about. Keerthana was in the dance; Ritu, her friend from Block C, had stopped even coming down to the courtyard. "You don't have to perform," Keerthana said on the stairs. "But would you do the music with me backstage? Nobody sees you there." Ritu thought about it for two days, then said yes. On the day, she pressed play at exactly the right moment for every song. Keerthana hugged her afterwards. "You came down. You did the whole thing." Later, on the steps, Keerthana said quietly, "You've stopped going to tuition too. Maybe tell your mum, and talk to someone who helps with this kind of fear?" Ritu nodded slowly.

qa.q: What job did Ritu do at the programme?
qa.a: She did the music backstage, pressing play at the right moment for every song.

qa.q: Why did Ritu take two days to decide?
qa.a: She was likely afraid of being seen and needed time to feel safe enough to agree.

qa.q: What did Keerthana suggest after noticing that Ritu had stopped going to tuition?
qa.a: Telling her mum and talking to someone who helps with this kind of fear.

qa.q: How might Keerthana feel when Ritu presses play at exactly the right moment?
qa.a: Keerthana probably feels proud and glad, which is why Keerthana hugs Ritu afterwards and says, "You did the whole thing."

grounding: A friend invites a fearful friend to a backstage role without pressure, celebrates the step, and gently suggests professional help.
